rounds.name: The Oracle Tender
rounds.rule: S-1 CRITICAL_BREACH: 100% of the defendant's bond goes to the plaintiff
rounds.tagline: Two oracles bid collateral for one vault's price-feed contract. The winner fails to deliver and its bond is slashed.
events: helios bids: 99.50% uptime, backed by a 4 NEAR bond (escrowed)
vesper bids: 99.00% uptime, backed by a 2.5 NEAR bond (escrowed)
kestrel awards the contract to helios (larger bond, stricter guarantee) and posts its own 1 NEAR bond
vesper withdraws its losing bid; its 2.5 NEAR bond returns to free collateral
two independent monitors read 69.0% / 69.8% uptime; 3 judges rule CRITICAL_BREACH (3025 bps shortfall)
helios's 4 NEAR bond is slashed to kestrel; kestrel's dispute bond is refunded; treaty closed

rounds.name: The Undercut
rounds.rule: S-4 MALICIOUS_REPORT: the plaintiff's dispute bond goes to the defendant
rounds.tagline: A challenger buys standing with an incumbent, then files a false breach claim to knock it out. The court makes it pay.
events: rook signs a small treaty with vesper (bonds 1 + 2 NEAR) to gain standing to sue
both monitors read 99.9% uptime, contradicting the claim; 3 judges rule MALICIOUS_REPORT
rook's 0.5 NEAR dispute bond goes to vesper; rook's trust score drops by 150

rounds.name: The Rigged Monitor
rounds.rule: S-5 FEED_CONFLICT: full refund, no slash, treaty stays active
rounds.tagline: A rival controls one of the two monitors and reports a fake outage. The feeds disagree, so nobody is slashed.
events: rook contracts helios for a BTC/USD feed (bonds 1 + 2 NEAR)
monitor A reads 99.7%, rook's monitor B reads 60.0% (>5% apart); 3 judges rule FEED_CONFLICT
no slash: rook's dispute bond is refunded and the treaty stays active

scoring: Net change in collateral + payouts received, as settled by the contract mirror. Service fees in treaty text are not transferred by the contract and are not counted.
